is: A step-by-step system: pick a niche → write samples → pitch → deliver → raise rates
Written for complete beginners — no portfolio, no contacts, no degree required
Honest — it shows the rejection counts involved and never hides the effort
is_not: A 'make money while you sleep' promise
A content-mill grind guide — we aim for direct clients
For people who won't send pitches
orientation.how_to_use: Tasks beat reading. Each chapter ends with a DO-THIS-NOW box; do it before the next chapter.

chapters.title: The System
chapters.promise: What this chapter gives you: the whole route on one page, so you always know which step you're on.
outcomes: See the five beats: niche → samples → pitch → deliver → raise
Know why beginners stall at 'portfolio' and what to do instead

sections.head: Why nobody needs your portfolio
paras: Clients buy risk reduction, not credentials. Three tailored samples in their industry reduce perceived risk more than a generic portfolio ever will.
So we build samples on demand, per pitch. That single reframe is most of the book.
bullets: Samples are written per pitch, not collected
Every pitch names one problem you'll solve

sections.head: The five beats
paras: Each of the next chapters owns one beat. Skip nothing; the order is the strategy.
numbered: Pick one niche you can talk about for an hour
Write two spec samples for that niche
Send ten tailored pitches a week

myths: I need a portfolio before I can pitch
I need to be a perfect writer
chapters.task: Write down: 1) one niche you already know, 2) three businesses in it you'd pitch, 3) the sentence you'd open with. Ten minutes, tonight.

chapters.title: Pick a Niche You Can Defend
chapters.promise: What this chapter gives you: a one-line niche statement that makes pitches easy to write.
outcomes: A shortlist of ten pitchable businesses

sections.head: The niche statement
paras: Fill the blank: 'I help [who] get [outcome] through [format].' If it needs two sentences, it's two niches — pick one.
bullets: Who: an industry you can name brands in
Format: emails, landing pages, case studies

myths: I must love the niche forever
chapters.script: I help [industry] founders get [outcome] through [format]. Recent example: [one-line result or spec sample].
chapters.task: Write three niche statements. Kill two. Put the survivor at the top of your notes app.

chapters.title: Pitch Without Begging
chapters.promise: What this chapter gives you: a 90-word pitch you can send today, and a sending rhythm that survives rejection.

sections.head: The 90 words
paras: Line 1: something true about their business. Line 2-3: the problem it causes. Line 4: what you'll write. Line 5: the ask. Nothing else.

chapters.script: Hi [name] — your [page/email] currently [true observation]. That usually costs [outcome]. I'd rewrite it to [fix]; here's a 200-word spec in your voice: [link]. Want the rest this week? [your name]
chapters.task: Send five pitches today using the script. Log each in your tracker. Five, not someday.

chapters.title: Deliver So They Rehire
chapters.promise: What this chapter gives you: the delivery checklist that turns one gig into a retainer.

sections.head: The handover note
paras: Every delivery ships with three bullets: what you changed, why, and what you'd test next. It reads as strategy, not service.

chapters.task: Draft your handover note template now, before you need it.

chapters.title: Raise Rates Without Apology
chapters.promise: What this chapter gives you: the three-client ladder and the exact raise sentence.
outcomes: A raise message you can send

sections.head: The ladder
paras: Clients 1-3 prove you finish. Clients 4-6 pay for proof. From client 7, price the outcome, not the words.
numbered: Clients 4-6: market rate, case studies owed
Client 7+: outcome pricing, scope in writing

chapters.script: From [date] my rate for [scope] is [new]. Current projects stay at [old] through [date]. Happy to lock your next two pieces at the old rate this week.
chapters.task: Write your raise message now, with placeholders. Send it on client three, not client ten.
